summary: Backend regression + new-feature testing for CyberShield iteration 2. Added /app/backend/tests/test_new_features.py (8 cases) covering PATCH /api/auth/me and the new attempts/progress fields on GET /api/labs. Ran the full backend suite (36 tests = 8 new + 28 regression). 36/36 PASSED (100%). All acceptance criteria met. The previously-reported HIGH issue (GET /api/payments/status returning 500) is now fixed — the endpoint gracefully falls back to the persisted DB record when Stripe responds with a validation error, as documented in the agent-to-agent context.

feature_verification.Existing endpoints (login, labs/start, l: PASS — full regression green; previously-failing payments/status now returns 200 with graceful fallback as intended
feature_verification.Seeded student 'Demo Student' name resto: PASS — explicit cleanup test PATCHes back to 'Demo Student'

critical_code_review_comments: server.py /api/payments/status now has the documented try/except fallback around stripe.get_checkout_status — looks correct and matches the intent stated in the agent-to-agent context.
ProfileUpdate model accepts only full_name; bio/avatar etc. can be added later without breaking the current schema (Optional, defaults to None).

Progress heuristic formula round(min(attempts/3, 0.85), 2) is straightforward and matches the spec; the +0.15 boost when an instance is live caps at 0.9 which is good (still < 1.0 reserved for solved).
server.py is now ~825 lines — over the 700-line guideline. Consider splitting into routers/* (auth, labs, payments, metrics) before adding more features.
seed_data_creation: Each run registers one TEST_progress_<uuid>@example.com user (used to assert clean attempts/progress state). Seeded student name is restored to 'Demo Student' by the final cleanup test. Cheap rows, not cleaned up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All backend features verified end-to-end at 100%. Use `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml` to re-run. Public URL comes from EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL in /app/frontend/.env (conftest.py handles fallback). Frontend has NOT been tested in this iteration; main agent specified 'backend only'.
